Prashant Paulose Global Lead, Envisioning Studio Nov 24, 2026 Every culture has its own visual language, and new tools are helping more storytellers share theirs with the world. We partnered with Women in Film India (WIF India) to launch the WIF India × Google Flow Filmathon , designed to democratize AI filmmaking and elevate talent beyond traditional production centers across India. Using Google Flow , our AI creative studio, participants paired their creative visions with AI to build original worlds from scratch. Five finalist short films recently debuted at the International Film Festival of India in Goa , bringing fresh, creative voices from across the country to the festival screen. The winners received their awards from the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Goa Dr. Pramod Sawant. Click through the carousel below to watch all five short films made with Google Flow and experience a bold new wave of independent storytelling. Haunted by visions of his late sister, a brother confronts grief and guilt in “Sikkal,” a chilling folk horror by Promita Banerjee, which took first place in the Filmathon. A stranger digging a mysterious hole sparks wild rumors across a quiet village in “Kuli,” a sharp Tamil black comedy by Syam Manohar, which came in second place. In “Pedals of Joy,” a heartfelt animation by Nikhil Shinde, an older brother in Mumbai sets out to fulfill a young boy’s dream. This film took third place. Aswathi Naduthodi’s visual essay “Bombay Mumbai - Vada Pav,” traces a city’s evolution through the everyday lives connected by one of its most popular street foods. In Srishti Chaudhary’s dialogue-free animation “Nazar,” a schoolgirl confronts the shadow of the unwanted gaze — and reclaims her sense of hope and power. The series is a continuation of Meta’s “Scam se Bacho” educational campaign in collaboration with MIB, Prasar Bharati, SEBI, and I4C. The series premieres on Instagram and will soon be available on Waves OTT, streaming platform launched by Prasar Bharati. Meta has partnered with The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (MIB), Prasar Bharati, Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), and Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to launch India’s first government-led public interest microdrama series on online scams. The series will premiere on Instagram and will soon be available on Waves OTT. The “Scam se Bacho” microdrama will be Waves OTT’s inaugural series with Meta that aims to educate audiences on some of the most prevalent online scams today, including fake job offers , investment and digital arrest scams, reiterating the importance of reporting suspicious behaviour online and encouraging users to call the national cybercrime helpline 1930 in case of fraud. Through an engaging, social-first approach, this initiative builds on the growing popularity of microdramas and demonstrates how innovative storytelling formats can be harnessed to make important public interest information more accessible and relatable. Scam Se Bacho: Raising Awareness Through A Whole-Of-Society Approach Building on Meta’s flagship anti-scam campaign “Scam se Bacho” – this latest initiative expands our educational efforts and reinforces the importance of tackling online scams through a whole-of-society approach by bringing together government agencies, creators and industry partners to reach audiences through India’s fastest-growing storytelling format. “India’s creator economy is witnessing remarkable growth, with new storytelling formats opening up opportunities for creators across the country. Waves OTT and Prasar Bharati are committed to nurturing these emerging formats while ensuring they can also be used to serve the public interest with microdramas like Scam se Bacho. This partnership brings together government, industry and creators to demonstrate how compelling storytelling can educate, inform and empower citizens, while strengthening India’s leadership in the evolving digital content landscape.” – Shri Gaurav Dwivedi, CEO of Prasar Bharati “Financial fraud continues to evolve rapidly, making awareness and timely information critical for investor protection. Through SEBI’s ongoing Samajh Se Investing Simple campaign, we aim to simplify investing and promote informed financial decisions. By using an emerging content format like microdramas, this collaboration will help people understand complex fraud patterns and encourage them to verify information before making financial decisions. We believe public awareness initiatives such as Scam Se Bacho play an important role in building financially aware and empowered citizens.” – Shri Sanjay C Purao, Executive Director, Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) “We are witnessing a rise in cyber frauds, including ‘digital arrest’ scams where criminals pose as law enforcement officials to intimidate citizens. These scams often rely on fear and urgency to prevent victims from verifying information. Public awareness and timely reporting are critical to combating such crimes. Campaigns like Scam Se Bacho play an important role in educating people on identifying red flags and taking immediate action.” – Shri Nishant Kumar, Director, Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) “Awareness works best when people recognise scams and warning signs in situations that feel familiar to them. Building on three successful editions of our ‘Scam Se Bacho’ campaign with government partners, this mobile-first microdrama series takes scam education beyond films and advisories. With Meta’s continued investments in technology, safety tools and a whole-of-society approach in collaboration with the government, industry and creators, we hope to help millions pause, verify and report before a scam can succeed.” – Aman Jain, Senior Director & Head of Public Policy, Meta India As part of the series, Meta has also released a comic strip driving awareness around common scam types like Investment scams and Digital Arrest scams – alerting people to spot signs early, urging them to pause, question and verify information that seems suspicious and always relying on safety tools to help avoid digital fraud. Launched in 2024, Meta’s “Scam se Bacho” awareness campaign reached more than 400 million users in India across Facebook and Instagram in 2024–2025. Through celebrity-led campaigns featuring Ayushmann Khurrana and Neena Gupta, as well as partnerships with regional creators, the initiative aims to empower people to combat online scams. Ongoing Collaboration With I4C To Educate Older Adults Last Month, Meta collaborated with I4C and Saksham Senior to launch specialized educational campaigns designed to help senior citizens identify and protect themselves against evolving scam archetypes. Launched as part of I4C’s Cybersecurity Awareness Month initiatives, the campaign aims to empower vulnerable demographics by featuring them as confident protagonists who actively champion scam awareness within their families and communities as opposed to traditional narratives that portray older adults merely as victims. articles.title: Meta Welcomes Loblaw as First Canadian Retail Partner to Muse
articles.excerpt: Starting today, Loblaw is bringing its catalogue to Muse as a partner connector, the first Canadian retailer to do so. Connectors are a big reason Muse can do so much. Canadians can connect their Muse to apps they already use, including Gmail, Google Calendar and Instagram, so it can help them manage email, coordinate schedules and draw on saved content to get everyday tasks done. With participating Loblaw banners, Canadian shoppers can now ask Muse to help with meal planning, build their basket and check-out, all in Muse. Muse can remember brand preferences and information like food allergies, making next week’s planning even easier. Making this technology work for everyone requires careful design and engineering to operate more safely. Muse runs on Muse Secure VM, a dedicated computer in the cloud that securely stores the data and credentials for the services you connect, while keeping passwords and payment methods out of the agent’s view. You choose what your Muse can access, and it checks with you before sensitive actions such as sending an email or making a purchase. To learn more about how we built safety into Muse, this post explains our approach in detail. Talk It Through With Muse: Voice Now Available in Canada At Connect 2026, we previewed real-time conversations with your Muse. Two weeks ago, we introduced voice and now we’re rolling it out in Canada in the Muse app on mobile, web and on Mac — just tap the phone icon in the top-right corner to start talking. Sometimes it’s easier to think out loud. With voice, you can talk through an idea with your Muse and let it take shape without worrying about the exact prompt. As your Muse speaks, the avatar uses subtle expressions and gestures that match the tone of the conversation. It reacts while you talk, so you can tell it’s following along. And you choose how present you want it to be: voice only, the avatar alongside your conversation, or full screen when you want to talk face to face. Design the Muse App, Just for You We also recently introduced spaces, an interactive way to build a more personalized Muse. A space is a custom experience you create inside Muse by describing your idea, like a holiday gift tracker, a daily word game, or a planning board for your next DIY project. It’s shaped around your routines, goals, and interests, and can be as practical or entertaining as you want. Add them to your sidebar, move them into your main tabs, hide the ones you don’t need right now, and schedule when they appear. For example, keep your weekly planner up front during the workweek, then swap it for your weekend plans on Saturday.
